blocks.text: Most first trips to Egypt follow the Nile. They begin in Cairo with the Pyramids of Giza and the main museums, then continue south to Luxor and Aswan. A Nile Cruise fits naturally between the two, and with a few extra days you can add Abu Simbel, Alexandria, or time on the Red Sea.

Our Egypt Tour Packages range from shorter Cairo stays to longer journeys covering several parts of the country. What is included varies by tour, but arrangements can include hotels, private transfers, domestic flights, guided sightseeing with licensed Egyptologist guides, daily breakfast, and a 3 or 4-night Nile Cruise. Private Tours and Customized Tours are available for travelers who want more control over dates, hotels, or the pace of the trip.

Egypt is not an easy destination to understand from a list of attractions alone. Cairo is busy and sprawling, Luxor feels like an open-air archaeological site, and Aswan moves at a noticeably slower pace. The Nile connects them, which is why combining these places usually makes more sense than visiting them as separate trips.

For most travelers, Cairo is the first introduction to Egypt. The Pyramids of Giza and Great Sphinx are the obvious starting points, but they are only part of what can be seen around the city.

Depending on the itinerary, your time in Cairo may also include the Grand Egyptian Museum, Saqqara, Memphis, and historic areas of the city. Two or three nights works well before flying south, although an extra day is useful if you want to see more than the main sites.

sections.heading: Travelling the Nile: Luxor to Aswan

blocks.text: This is where an Egypt itinerary works differently from most of our other destinations. Rather than repeatedly packing, driving, and changing hotels, part of the journey can be made by boat.

Nile Cruises commonly sail Luxor to Aswan over 4 nights or Aswan to Luxor over 3 nights, depending on the itinerary and departure schedule. Stops along the way can include Edfu and Kom Ombo, with sightseeing in Luxor and Aswan arranged around the cruise.

In Luxor, visits typically include Karnak Temple and the Valley of the Kings, along with other sites on the East and West Banks. Aswan has a different atmosphere altogether, with Philae Temple, the Nile islands, and a more relaxed waterfront setting.
If your schedule allows it, yes. Abu Simbel is south of Aswan, so it needs additional travel time rather than being something you simply stop at along the Nile Cruise route.

The temples were built during the reign of Ramesses II and moved to their present location in the 1960s to protect them from the rising waters created by the Aswan High Dam. Some of our Egypt Tours include Abu Simbel in the itinerary; on others, it can be added separately.

sections.heading: How Many Days Do You Need in Egypt?

blocks.text: For Cairo alone, four or five days can work well. If this is your first visit and you also want to see Luxor and Aswan, allowing around eight to ten days gives you much more room to include a Nile Cruise without moving every day.
With additional time, Alexandria can be added from Cairo, while Hurghada or another Red Sea destination works well at the end of a cultural tour if you want a few quieter days before flying home.
The important thing is not to add places simply because they fit on a map. Cairo, a Nile Cruise, Luxor, Aswan, and Abu Simbel already make for a full first trip.

October through April is generally the easier period for long days of archaeological sightseeing, particularly in Luxor and Aswan. December through February are popular months, so hotels and Nile Cruises can also be busier during this period.
Egypt can still be visited during the summer, but temperatures in Upper Egypt are much higher. Sightseeing often needs to start earlier in the day, while Red Sea resorts operate throughout the year.

sections.heading: Adding Egypt to a Longer Trip

blocks.text: Egypt also works well as the final or starting country in a regional itinerary. The important part is allowing enough time in each country rather than adding another border crossing simply to fit more places into the same holiday.
See our Turkey & Egypt Tours, Greece & Egypt Tours, or Turkey, Greece & Egypt Tours if you are considering a multi-country journey.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for an Egypt tour?
faqs.a: Most first-time visitors need eight to ten days to explore Cairo, Giza, Luxor, Aswan, and the main Nile Cruise sites without rushing. Twelve to fifteen days allows time for Abu Simbel, Alexandria, or a Red Sea stay. Shorter four- to six-day itineraries usually focus on Cairo and one additional destination.

faqs.q: What is the best Egypt itinerary for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: A well-balanced first Egypt itinerary normally includes two or three nights in Cairo, a domestic flight to Aswan or Luxor, and a three- or four-night Nile Cruise. Abu Simbel can be added from Aswan, while travelers with additional time may finish with Alexandria, Hurghada, or Sharm El-Sheikh.

faqs.q: Is a Nile Cruise worth including in an Egypt tour?
faqs.a: Yes. A Nile Cruise provides a comfortable way to travel between Luxor and Aswan while visiting major temples at Edfu, Kom Ombo, Luxor, and Aswan. It combines accommodation, transportation, meals, river scenery, and guided sightseeing, making it especially practical for first-time visitors exploring the archaeological highlights of Upper Egypt.

faqs.q: Should I take a Nile Cruise from Luxor or Aswan?
faqs.a: Both directions visit many of the same major sites. Luxor-to-Aswan cruises commonly operate for four nights, while Aswan-to-Luxor programs often last three nights. The best direction depends on cruise departure days, domestic flight schedules, cabin availability, and your wider itinerary rather than one route being universally better.

faqs.q: Are your Egypt tours private or group based?
faqs.a: Magnificent Travel offers Private Tours, Small Group Tours, Nile Cruise packages, and Customized Tours. Private itineraries include greater flexibility, personal guiding, and privately arranged transportation. Some cruise excursions or scheduled programs may operate with other travelers. The exact service type and group arrangement are clearly identified in each confirmed proposal.

faqs.q: Can I customize an Egypt tour itinerary?
faqs.a: Yes. Egypt itineraries can be customized according to your travel dates, preferred destinations, hotel category, cruise standard, sightseeing interests, budget, and desired pace. You may extend Cairo, add Abu Simbel, include Alexandria, choose a Red Sea resort, or combine Egypt with Turkey, Greece, Jordan, or another available destination.

Licensed English-speaking Egyptologist guides are provided for the sightseeing services specified in the confirmed itinerary. They explain the historical, archaeological, and cultural importance of temples, tombs, museums, and ancient sites. Guiding arrangements may differ during free days, optional activities, resort stays, or onboard periods without scheduled excursions.

faqs.q: What is normally included in an Egypt tour package?
faqs.a: Most packages include selected hotel accommodation, daily breakfast, specified transfers, guided sightseeing, listed entrance fees, and domestic transportation shown in the itinerary. Nile Cruise programs frequently include full-board meals. International flights, travel insurance, tips, personal expenses, optional activities, and services not specifically listed are normally excluded.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to visit Egypt?
faqs.a: October through April generally provides the most comfortable temperatures for cultural sightseeing and Nile Cruises. December through February is the busiest period, with mild days and cooler evenings. May through September can be extremely hot in Upper Egypt, although Red Sea resorts remain popular and early morning sightseeing can still be arranged.

faqs.q: Is Egypt suitable for families with children?
faqs.a: Egypt can be highly rewarding for families, especially when the itinerary balances archaeological sightseeing with rest time, pools, interactive experiences, and a Red Sea stay. Private Tours are often most convenient because daily schedules can be adjusted. Parents should consider children’s ages, heat tolerance, walking distances, and preferred travel pace.

faqs.q: Is Egypt suitable for senior travelers?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the itinerary is planned around mobility, climate, and a comfortable pace. Private transportation, carefully selected hotels, suitable cruise cabins, and shorter sightseeing periods can improve comfort. Travelers should advise the tour operator about walking limitations, dietary requirements, medical considerations, or room-access needs before finalizing the arrangements.

faqs.q: Should I visit Hurghada or Sharm El-Sheikh?
faqs.a: Hurghada connects conveniently with Luxor by road and works well after a Nile Cruise. Sharm El-Sheikh is normally combined with Cairo by domestic flight and provides access to Sinai experiences. Both offer resorts, snorkeling, and diving. The better choice depends on your itinerary, preferred hotel, marine interests, and available travel time.

faqs.q: Is Abu Simbel worth adding to an Egypt tour?
faqs.a: Abu Simbel is highly recommended for travelers interested in ancient architecture, archaeology, and monumental temple design. It is usually visited from Aswan by road or domestic flight. Although the excursion requires additional travel time, many visitors consider the temples among the most memorable sites included in a comprehensive Egypt itinerary.

faqs.q: Can Egypt be combined with Turkey, Greece, or Jordan?
faqs.a: Yes. Multi Country Tours can combine Egypt with Turkey, Greece, or Jordan through coordinated regional flights, hotels, transfers, and local sightseeing. Popular options include Turkey and Egypt Tours, Greece and Egypt Tours, and Egypt and Jordan Tours. A combined itinerary usually requires at least ten to fourteen days, depending on the selected destinations.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa to travel to Egypt?
faqs.a: Visa requirements depend on nationality, passport type, entry point, travel purpose, and current government regulations. Travelers should confirm the latest requirements with the relevant Egyptian authority or diplomatic mission before departure. Magnificent Travel can provide general planning guidance, but each traveler remains responsible for obtaining the correct travel documentation.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book an Egypt tour?
faqs.a: Booking three to six months in advance is recommended for travel between October and April, particularly during Christmas, New Year, Easter, and other popular periods. Early reservations provide a better choice of hotels, cruise cabins, domestic flights, and licensed guides. Last-minute arrangements may be possible but usually offer less flexibility.

faqs.q: Are domestic flights included in Egypt tour packages?
faqs.a: Domestic flights are included only when they are specifically listed in the confirmed itinerary and quotation. Common flight sectors include Cairo to Luxor, Cairo to Aswan, Cairo to Sharm El-Sheikh, and selected Abu Simbel services. Flight times, baggage allowances, availability, and ticket conditions should be reviewed before booking.

faqs.q: Is Egypt safe for organized tours?
faqs.a: Most visitors explore Egypt through established tourism routes, licensed guides, professional drivers, and coordinated transportation. Conditions can change, so travelers should review current official travel advice before departure and follow local guidance during the trip. A professionally organized itinerary reduces logistical uncertainty and provides local assistance when plans require adjustment.
